structures.name: L-threonine
structures.definition: An optically active form of threonine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

structures.why: The residue that forms disulfide bridges.
structures.name: L-cysteine
structures.definition: An optically active form of cysteine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

structures.why: The initiator residue of every eukaryotic translation.
structures.name: L-methionine
structures.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of methionine.

structures.why: The N-linked glycosylation site.
structures.name: L-asparagine
structures.definition: An optically active form of asparagine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

structures.why: The main nitrogen carrier in blood.
structures.name: L-glutamine
structures.definition: An optically active form of glutamine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

structures.why: Acidic; the second member of the catalytic triad.
structures.name: L-aspartic acid
structures.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of aspartic acid.

structures.why: Acidic, and the principal excitatory neurotransmitter.
structures.name: L-glutamic acid
structures.definition: An optically active form of glutamic acid having <small>L</small>-configuration.

structures.why: Basic; the residue whose acetylation writes the histone code.
structures.name: L-lysine
structures.definition: An <small>L</small>-α-amino acid; the <small>L</small>-isomer of lysine.

structures.why: The most basic residue, and the substrate of nitric oxide synthase.
structures.name: L-arginine
structures.definition: An <small>L</small>-α-amino acid that is the <small>L</small>-isomer of arginine.

structures.why: The only side chain that titrates at physiological pH.
structures.name: L-histidine
structures.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of the amino acid histidine.

structures.why: The energy currency of the cell.
structures.name: ATP
structures.definition: An adenosine 5'-phosphate in which the 5'-phosphate is a triphosphate group. It is involved in the transportation of chemical energy during metabolic pathways.

structures.why: The other half of that currency.
structures.name: ADP
structures.definition: A purine ribonucleoside 5'-diphosphate having adenine as the nucleobase.

structures.why: The nucleotide the energy charge is measured against.
structures.name: adenosine 5'-monophosphate
structures.definition: A purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate having adenine as the nucleobase.

structures.why: The oxidised hydride acceptor of catabolism.
structures.name: NAD(+)
structures.definition: The oxidised form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide found in all living cells. In metabolism, NAD<small><sup>+</small></sup> is involved in redox reactions, carrying electrons from one reaction to another.

structures.why: Its reduced form: the electrons the respiratory chain consumes.
structures.name: NADH
structures.definition: A coenzyme found in all living cells; consists of two nucleotides joined through their 5'-phosphate groups, with one nucleotide containing an adenine base and the other containing nicotinamide.

structures.why: The anabolic sibling, kept in a separate redox pool.
structures.name: NADP(+)

structures.why: The two-electron flavin cofactor of succinate dehydrogenase.
structures.name: FAD
structures.definition: A flavin adenine dinucleotide in which the substituent at position 10 of the flavin nucleus is a 5'-adenosyldiphosphoribityl group.

structures.why: The one-flavin cofactor of complex I.
structures.name: FMN
structures.definition: A flavin mononucleotide that is riboflavin (vitamin B<small><sub>2</sub></small>) in which the primary hydroxy group has been converted to its dihydrogen phosphate ester.

structures.why: The universal acyl carrier.
structures.name: coenzyme A
structures.definition: A thiol comprising a panthothenate unit in phosphoric anhydride linkage with a 3',5'-adenosine diphosphate unit; and an aminoethanethiol unit.

structures.why: The junction of every catabolic pathway.
structures.name: acetyl-CoA
structures.definition: An acyl-CoA having acetyl as its S-acetyl component.

structures.why: The iron porphyrin of haemoglobin, myoglobin and the cytochromes.
structures.name: heme b
structures.definition: A metalloprotoporphyrin in which the four pyrrole nitrogens of the protoporphyrin moiety are coordinated to iron. It is the most abundant of the heme compounds.

structures.why: The magnesium porphyrin that starts photosynthesis.
structures.name: chlorophyll a

structures.why: The cofactor of essentially all amino-acid transaminations.
structures.name: pyridoxal 5'-phosphate
structures.definition: The monophosphate ester obtained by condensation of phosphoric acid with the primary hydroxy group of pyridoxal.

structures.why: The cofactor of pyruvate dehydrogenase.
structures.name: thiamine(1+) diphosphate
structures.definition: A thiamine phosphate that is thiamine(1+) in which the hydroxy group has been replaced by a diphosphate group. It is the active form of vitamin B<small><sub>1</sub></small> and an essential cofactor for enzymes in key metabolic pathways.

structures.why: The carboxyl carrier, and half of the tightest binding pair in biotech.
structures.name: biotin
structures.definition: An organic heterobicyclic compound that consists of 2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazole having a valeric acid substituent attached to the tetrahydrothiophene ring. The parent of the class of biotins.

structures.why: The universal methyl donor.
structures.name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine
structures.definition: A sulfonium compound that is the S-adenosyl derivative of L-methionine. It is an intermediate in the metabolic pathway of methionine.

structures.why: Coenzyme Q, the mobile electron carrier of the inner membrane.
structures.name: coenzyme Q10
structures.definition: A ubiquinone having a side chain of 10 isoprenoid units. In the naturally occurring isomer, all isoprenyl double bonds are in the E- configuration.

structures.why: The chromophore of rhodopsin: vision, as a molecule.
structures.name: retinal
structures.definition: An enal that consists of 3,7-dimethyl-9-nona-2,4,6,8-tetraenal (double bond geometry unspecified) carrying a 2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl group at the 9-position.

structures.why: Blood sugar, in the ring form it actually adopts.
structures.name: D-glucopyranose
structures.definition: A glucopyranose having <small>D</small>-configuration.

structures.why: The anomer that polymerises into cellulose.
structures.name: beta-D-glucose
structures.definition: <small>D</small>-Glucopyranose with β configuration at the anomeric centre.

structures.why: The anomer that polymerises into starch and glycogen.
structures.name: alpha-D-glucose
structures.definition: <small>D</small>-Glucopyranose having α-configuration at the anomeric centre.

structures.why: The ketose of the fruit sugar, and of sucrose.
structures.name: beta-D-fructofuranose

structures.why: The epimer whose metabolism fails in galactosaemia.
structures.name: beta-D-galactose
structures.definition: A <small>D</small>-galactopyranose having β configuration at the anomeric centre.

structures.why: The pentose of RNA and of every nucleotide cofactor.
structures.name: beta-D-ribose
structures.definition: A <small>D</small>-ribofuranose in which the anomeric centre has β-configuration.

structures.why: The pentose that makes DNA chemically stable.
structures.name: 2-deoxy-D-ribose
structures.definition: A deoxypentose that is <small>D</small>-ribose in which the hydroxy group at position C-2 is replaced by hydrogen.

structures.why: Table sugar: the glucose-fructose disaccharide.
structures.name: sucrose
structures.definition: A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.

structures.why: Milk sugar, and the reason lactase persistence is a famous allele.
structures.name: lactose
structures.definition: A glycosylglucose disaccharide, found most notably in milk, that consists of <small>D</small>-galactose and <small>D</small>-glucose fragments bonded through a β-1→4 glycosidic linkage. The glucose fragment can be in either the α- or β-pyranose form, whereas the galactose fragment can only have the β-pyranose form.

structures.why: The disaccharide starch digestion produces.
structures.name: maltose
structures.definition: A glycosylglucose consisting of two <small>D</small>-glucopyranose units connected by an α-(1→4)-linkage.

structures.why: The sugar of high-mannose N-glycans.
structures.name: alpha-D-mannose
structures.definition: <small>D</small>-Mannopyranose having α-configuration at the anomeric centre.

structures.why: The unit of chitin and of the peptidoglycan backbone.
structures.name: N-acetyl-D-glucosamine
structures.definition: The D isomer of N-acetylglucosamine.

structures.why: Purine; pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds.
structures.name: adenine
structures.definition: The parent compound of the 6-aminopurines, composed of a purine having an amino group at C-6.

structures.why: Purine; pairs with cytosine through three.
structures.name: guanine
structures.definition: A 2-aminopurine carrying a 6-oxo substituent.

structures.why: Pyrimidine, and the base whose methylation carries epigenetic marks.
structures.name: cytosine
structures.definition: An aminopyrimidine that is pyrimidin-2-one having the amino group located at position 4.

structures.why: The pyrimidine DNA uses instead of uracil.
structures.name: thymine
structures.definition: A pyrimidine nucleobase that is uracil in which the hydrogen at position 5 is replaced by a methyl group.

structures.why: The pyrimidine RNA uses instead of thymine.
structures.name: uracil
structures.definition: A common and naturally occurring pyrimidine nucleobase in which the pyrimidine ring is substituted with two oxo groups at positions 2 and 4. Found in RNA, it base pairs with adenine and replaces thymine during DNA transcription.

structures.why: The nucleoside, and a signalling molecule in its own right.
structures.name: adenosine
structures.definition: A ribonucleoside composed of a molecule of adenine attached to a ribofuranose moiety via a β‒N<small><sup>9</small></sup>-glycosidic bond.

structures.why: The nucleoside behind GTP and the G protein switch.
structures.name: guanosine
structures.definition: A purine nucleoside in which guanine is attached to ribofuranose via a β-N9-glycosidic bond.

structures.why: The pyrimidine nucleoside of CTP and CDP-lipids.
structures.name: cytidine
structures.definition: A pyrimidine nucleoside in which cytosine is attached to ribofuranose via a β-N1-glycosidic bond.

structures.why: The nucleoside of UTP and of UDP-glucose.
structures.name: uridine
structures.definition: A ribonucleoside composed of a molecule of uracil attached to a ribofuranose moiety via a β‒N<small><sup>1</small></sup>-glycosidic bond.

structures.why: The deoxynucleoside used to label replicating DNA.
structures.name: thymidine
structures.definition: A pyrimidine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside having thymine as the nucleobase.

structures.why: The nucleotide that powers translation and every G protein.
structures.name: GTP

structures.why: The second messenger that made the term necessary.
structures.name: 3',5'-cyclic AMP
structures.definition: A 3',5'-cyclic purine nucleotide having having adenine as the nucleobase.

structures.why: The sterol of every animal membrane, and of every steroid hormone.
structures.name: cholesterol
structures.definition: A cholestanoid consisting of cholestane having a double bond at the 5,6-position as well as a 3β-hydroxy group.

structures.why: The commonest saturated fatty acid, and the product of fatty-acid synthase.
structures.name: hexadecanoic acid
structures.definition: A straight-chain, sixteen-carbon, saturated long-chain fatty acid.

structures.why: The commonest monounsaturated fatty acid.
structures.name: oleic acid
structures.definition: An octadec-9-enoic acid in which the double bond at C-9 has Z (cis) stereochemistry.

structures.why: An essential fatty acid: the body cannot make it.
structures.name: linoleic acid
structures.definition: An octadecadienoic acid in which the two double bonds are at positions 9 and 12 and have Z (cis) stereochemistry.

structures.why: The precursor of prostaglandins, and the substrate aspirin blocks.
structures.name: arachidonic acid
structures.definition: A long-chain fatty acid that is a C20, polyunsaturated fatty acid having four (Z)-double bonds at positions 5, 8, 11 and 14.

structures.why: The backbone of every triglyceride and phospholipid.
structures.name: glycerol
structures.definition: A triol with a structure of propane substituted at positions 1, 2 and 3 by hydroxy groups.

structures.why: The backbone of sphingolipids and the myelin sheath.
structures.name: sphingosine
structures.definition: A sphing-4-enine in which the double bond is trans.

structures.why: The fight-or-flight catecholamine.
structures.name: (R)-adrenaline
structures.definition: The R-enantiomer of adrenaline. It is a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands resulting in the 'fight-or-flight' response.

structures.why: The sympathetic neurotransmitter and its close relative.
structures.name: noradrenaline
structures.definition: A catecholamine in which C-1 of the aminoethyl side-chain is hydroxy-substituted.

structures.why: The catecholamine of reward, and of Parkinson disease.
structures.name: dopamine
structures.definition: Catechol in which the hydrogen at position 4 is substituted by a 2-aminoethyl group.

structures.why: The monoamine SSRIs act on.
structures.name: serotonin
structures.definition: A primary amino compound that is the 5-hydroxy derivative of tryptamine.

structures.why: The neuromuscular junction transmitter.
structures.name: acetylcholine
structures.definition: Actylcholine is an ester of acetic acid and choline, which acts as a neurotransmitter.

structures.why: The mediator of allergy and gastric acid secretion.
structures.name: histamine
structures.definition: A member of the class of imidazoles that is 1H-imidazole substituted at position C-4 by a 2-aminoethyl group.

structures.why: The principal inhibitory neurotransmitter.
structures.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid
structures.definition: A γ-amino acid that is butanoic acid with the amino substituent located at C-4.

structures.why: An osmolyte and methyl donor, kept as a contrast to glycine itself.
structures.name: glycine betaine
structures.definition: The amino acid betaine derived from glycine.

structures.why: The hormone of the circadian phase.
structures.name: melatonin
structures.definition: A member of the class of acetamides that is acetamide in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen atom is replaced by a 2-(5-methoxy-1H-indol-3-yl)ethyl group. It is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in humans.

structures.why: The gas that acts as a signal, and the reason NO synthase exists.
structures.name: nitric oxide
structures.definition: A nitrogen oxide which is a free radical, each molecule of which consists of one nitrogen and one oxygen atom.

structures.why: The principal androgen.
structures.name: testosterone
structures.definition: An androstanoid having 17β-hydroxy and 3-oxo groups, together with unsaturation at C-4‒C-5..

structures.why: The principal oestrogen, and the ligand of 3ERT.
structures.name: estradiol
structures.definition: A 3-hydroxy steroid that is estra-1,3,5(10)-triene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 17.

structures.why: The glucocorticoid of the stress axis.
structures.name: cortisol
structures.definition: A 17α-hydroxy-C<small><sub>21</sub></small>-steroid that is pregn-4-ene substituted by oxo groups at positions 3 and 20 and hydroxy groups at positions 11, 17 and 21. Cortisol is a corticosteroid hormone or glucocorticoid produced by zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex, which is a part of the adrenal gland. It is usually referred to as the "stress hormone" as it is involved in response to stress and anxiety, controlled by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH). It increases blood pressure and blood sugar, and reduces immune responses.

structures.why: The steroid of the luteal phase and of pregnancy.
structures.name: progesterone
structures.definition: A C<small><sub>21</sub></small>-steroid hormone in which a pregnane skeleton carries oxo substituents at positions 3 and 20 and is unsaturated at C(4)-C(5). As a hormone, it is involved in the female menstrual cycle, pregnancy and embryogenesis of humans and other species.

structures.why: The iodinated hormone that sets basal metabolic rate.
structures.name: thyroxine
structures.definition: An iodothyronine compound having iodo substituents at the 3-, 3'-, 5- and 5'-positions.

structures.why: The mineralocorticoid that controls sodium retention.
structures.name: aldosterone
structures.definition: A pregnane-based steroidal hormone produced by the outer-section (zona glomerulosa) of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland, and acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts of the kidney to cause the conservation of sodium, secretion of potassium, increased water retention, and increased blood pressure. The overall effect of aldosterone is to increase reabsorption of ions and water in the kidney.

structures.why: Irreversible COX inhibitor: the drug seen bound in 1PTH.
structures.name: acetylsalicylic acid
structures.definition: A member of the class of benzoic acids that is salicylic acid in which the hydrogen that is attached to the phenolic hydroxy group has been replaced by an acetoxy group. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with cyclooxygenase inhibitor activity.

structures.why: The analgesic whose mechanism is still argued about.
structures.name: paracetamol
structures.definition: A member of the class of phenols that is 4-aminophenol in which one of the hydrogens attached to the amino group has been replaced by an acetyl group.

structures.why: The reversible NSAID taught beside aspirin.
structures.name: ibuprofen
structures.definition: A monocarboxylic acid that is propionic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 2 is substituted by a 4-(2-methylpropyl)phenyl group.

structures.why: Adenosine receptor antagonist; the most consumed psychoactive compound.
structures.name: caffeine
structures.definition: A trimethylxanthine in which the three methyl groups are located at positions 1, 3, and 7. A purine alkaloid that occurs naturally in tea and coffee.

structures.why: The opioid agonist that named the receptor.
structures.name: morphine
structures.definition: A morphinane alkaloid that is a highly potent opiate analgesic psychoactive drug. Morphine acts directly on the central nervous system (CNS) to relieve pain but has a high potential for addiction, with tolerance and both physical and psychological dependence developing rapidly. Morphine is the most abundant opiate found in Papaver somniferum (the opium poppy).

structures.why: The beta-lactam that started antibiotics.
structures.name: benzylpenicillin
structures.definition: A penicillin in which the substituent at position 6 of the penam ring is a phenylacetamido group.

structures.why: The aminopenicillin actually prescribed today.
structures.name: amoxicillin
structures.definition: A penicillin in which the substituent at position 6 of the penam ring is a 2-amino-2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)acetamido group.

structures.why: The first targeted kinase inhibitor; seen bound in 1IEP.
structures.name: imatinib
structures.definition: A benzamide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 4-[(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl]benzoic acid with the primary aromatic amino group of 4-methyl-N3-[4-(pyridin-3-yl)pyrimidin-2-yl]benzene-1,3-diamine. Used (as its mesylate salt) for treatment of chronic myelogenous leukemia and gastrointestinal stromal tumours.

structures.why: The neuraminidase inhibitor of 2QWE.
structures.name: oseltamivir
structures.definition: A cyclohexenecarboxylate ester that is the ethyl ester of oseltamivir acid. An antiviral prodrug (it is hydrolysed to the active free carboxylic acid in the liver), it is used to slow the spread of influenza.

structures.why: The antifolate of 1DHF.
structures.name: methotrexate

structures.why: The selective oestrogen receptor modulator of 3ERT.
structures.name: tamoxifen

structures.why: The acetylcholinesterase inhibitor of 1EVE.
structures.name: donepezil
structures.definition: A racemate comprising equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-donepezil. A centrally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, its main therapeutic use is in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease where it is used to increase cortical acetylcholine.

structures.why: The HIV protease inhibitor of 1HXB.
structures.name: saquinavir
structures.definition: An aspartic acid derivative obtained by formal condensation of the primary amino group of (2S,3R)-4-[(3S,4aS,8aS)-3-(tert-butylcarbamoyl)octahydroisoquinolin-2(1H)-yl]-3-hydroxy-1-phenylbutan-2-ylamine with the carboxy group of N2(-quinolin-2-ylcarbonyl)-L-asparagine. An inhibitor of HIV-1 protease.

structures.why: The statin, and the largest-selling drug in history.
structures.name: atorvastatin
structures.definition: A dihydroxy monocarboxylic acid that is a member of the drug class known as statins, used primarily for lowering blood cholesterol and for preventing cardiovascular diseases.

structures.why: First-line therapy in type 2 diabetes.
structures.name: metformin
structures.definition: A member of the class of guanidines that is biguanide the carrying two methyl substituents at position 1.

structures.why: The vitamin K antagonist, and a pharmacogenetics classic.
structures.name: (S)-warfarin
structures.definition: A 4-hydroxy-3-(3-oxo-1-phenylbutyl)-2H-1-benzopyran-2-one that has (S)-configuration (the racemate is warfarin, an anticoagulant drug and rodenticide).

structures.why: The fluoroquinolone that targets DNA gyrase.
structures.name: ciprofloxacin
structures.definition: A quinolone that is quinolin-4(1H)-one bearing cyclopropyl, carboxylic acid, fluoro and piperazin-1-yl substituents at positions 1, 3, 6 and 7, respectively.

structures.why: The DNA intercalator of many chemotherapy regimens.
structures.name: doxorubicin

structures.why: The microtubule stabiliser: the ligand side of 1TUB.
structures.name: paclitaxel
structures.definition: A tetracyclic diterpenoid isolated originally from the bark of the Pacific yew tree, Taxus brevifolia. It is a mitotic inhibitor used in cancer chemotherapy. Note that the use of the former generic name 'taxol' is now limited, as Taxol is a registered trade mark.

structures.why: The microtubule destabiliser, and the gout drug.
structures.name: colchicine
structures.definition: An alkaloid that is a carbotricyclic compound comprising 5,6,7,9-tetrahydrobenzo[a]heptalene having four methoxy substituents at the 1-, 2-, 3- and 10-positions as well as an oxo group at the 9-position and an acetamido group at the 7-position. It has been isolated from the plants belonging to genus Colchicum.

structures.why: The solvent, and the molecule every structure is full of.
structures.name: water
structures.definition: An oxygen hydride consisting of an oxygen atom that is covalently bonded to two hydrogen atoms

structures.why: The nitrogen waste product, and the classic denaturant.
structures.name: urea
structures.definition: A carbonyl group with two C-bound amine groups. The commercially available fertilizer has an analysis of 46-0-0 (N-P2O5-K2O).

structures.why: The alcohol, and the substrate of alcohol dehydrogenase.
structures.name: ethanol
structures.definition: A primary alcohol that is ethane in which one of the hydrogens is substituted by a hydroxy group.

structures.why: Vitamin C, the cofactor of collagen prolyl hydroxylase.
structures.name: L-ascorbic acid
structures.definition: The <small>L</small>-enantiomer of ascorbic acid and conjugate acid of <small>L</small>-ascorbate.

structures.why: What haemoglobin carries.
structures.name: dioxygen

structures.why: What carbonic anhydrase hydrates.
structures.name: carbon dioxide
structures.definition: A one-carbon compound with formula CO<small><sub>2</sub></small> in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food.

structures.why: The buffer of blood pH.
structures.name: hydrogencarbonate
structures.definition: The carbon oxoanion resulting from the removal of a proton from carbonic acid.

structures.why: The end product of anaerobic glycolysis.
structures.name: (S)-lactic acid
structures.definition: An optically active form of lactic acid having (S)-configuration.

structures.why: The junction between glycolysis and the TCA cycle.
structures.name: pyruvate
structures.definition: A 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of pyruvic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

structures.why: The first intermediate of the cycle named after it.
structures.name: citric acid
structures.definition: A tricarboxylic acid that is propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 2. It is an important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms.

structures.why: The purine end product that crystallises in gout.
structures.name: 7,9-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6,8(3H)-trione
structures.definition: An oxopurine in which the purine ring is substituted by oxo groups at positions 2, 6, and 8.

structures.why: The phosphagen buffer of muscle ATP.
structures.name: creatine
structures.definition: A glycine derivative having methyl and amidino groups attached to the nitrogen.
